title: Sprint redlines: rapid eval + scriptlets
content:
Purpose: quick, surgical checklist + micro-scripts to use during 15–30m redline sprints. Not a finished playbook — personal notes and fallback language.

Toplines to flag in every draft (fast heuristics):
- Liability cap: prefer contract value cap or 2x fees for initial term. Absolute no on unlimited. Quick ask: "Cap on direct damages limited to the greater of fees paid in prior 12 months or $1,000,000." If counterparty insists on higher, escalate.
- Indemnity: carve out model output / training vs customer-provided data. If customer insists on broad indemnity, require reciprocity and narrow scope to third-party IP claims only. Script: "We can accept IP indemnity for third-party claims alleging the product infringes an issued patent or copyrighted code, but not for outputs generated based on customer prompts or public data."
- Data ownership / usage for training: default position = customer retains ownership; vendor gets narrow rights to operate/serve. If customer asks to use data for model training, require anonymization + opt-in + fee + explicit security commitments. Quick line: "Any use of customer data for model training requires mutual written consent and agreed SLA for deletion/anonymization."
- Model output IP: push for customer ownership of their output, or at minimum unlimited rights to use internally/externally. If vendor retains rights, ask for explicit carveouts and non-exclusive license back to customer.
- Subprocessors / subprocessors list: require 30 days notice and opt-out for high-risk regions. Script: "We require notice for new subprocessors and the right to reasonably object; critical subprocessors must meet SOC2+ and EU adequacy or equivalent safeguards."
- Audit rights & compliance: limit third-party audit requests to reasonable frequency and scope. Prefer request -> mutual discovery call -> redacted evidence. Avoid on-site forensic access demands.
- Security controls & KMS: require keys-in-customer-control for private deployments; for hosted, require clear KMS integration and encryption-at-rest details. Ask for attestation for HSM usage if required by customer compliance.
- Data residency: if customer requires EU/UK residency, map to our region-specific deployment offering; fallback = pseudonymization + strict contract terms + breach SLA. Quick: "Data processing to occur in region X unless otherwise agreed in writing."
- Termination & data return/erase: must define a clear retention schedule, export format, and a 30–90 day grace period with assistance. Script: "On termination vendor will provide data export (JSON/CSV) and certify deletion of customer data from production and backups within 60 days."
- SLA, credits & remedies: avoid liquidated damages; prefer credits. Insert formula for credits tied to downtime per route. Keep a short escalation path for persistent degradations and auto-fallback options to lower-cost models.
- Export controls & sanctions: require representations re: compliance with US/EU sanctions; make sure jurisdiction-specific obligations don't create broad buyer obligations.
- Confidentiality exceptions: carve out aggregated/ de-identified telemetry for product improvement. Must be non-reversible and cannot contain PII.

Rapid negotiation scripts (short):
- If counterparty demands unlimited liability: "We can’t accept unlimited liability. We can negotiate a higher capped exposure tied to committed spend — what is the commercial rationale for the request?"
- If they want broad training rights: "We need written consent and a commercial arrangement for training use; can we scope to non-production/aggregated data only?"
- On KYC / on-prem inspections: "We’re open to remote audits and evidence sharing; full on-site access requires a separate SOW and 30-day notice."

Minimal acceptable redlines (my quick checklist when triaging):
- Liability cap: present (not unlimited).
- Data return/erase: acceptable timeline (<=90 days).
- Indemnity scope: limited to third-party IP claims.
- Data usage: no training without consent.
- Subprocessor notice: present.
- SLA: measurable and credit-only remedy.

Escalation triggers (call legal + sales):
- Counterparty will not accept any cap OR asks for unlimited consequential damages.
- Wants broad indemnity covering regulatory fines or bodily injury.
- Insists on indefinite rights to derivative model training that include customer private data.
- Demands unfettered audit/on-site for our production environment.

Notes-to-self / negotiation heuristics:
- Ask commercial team for the 3 most important commercial levers for this customer before major concessions. Often we can trade higher cap for committed revenue or longer term.
- Use templates but tailor to region (EU/UK needs stronger data residency + SCCs).
- Keep scripts short for CS/AE use — they will paste during slack threads with counsel.
- Track any carveouts we give in a running ticket (LEGAL-XXXX) so we can propagate to future deals.

Open questions / items to follow up:
- Can UX confirm expected export format types customers ask for? (CSV, JSON) - ping platform-eng.
- For one-off canary customers, do we have an expedited KMS onboarding checklist? - ops + infra.
- Determine threshold for revenue-linked cap escalations (need guidance from finance).

Quick example redline snippets to paste (micro-script library):
1) Liability cap: "Notwithstanding any other provision, the aggregate liability of Vendor for direct damages shall not exceed the greater of (a) fees paid by Customer to Vendor under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to liability; or (b) $1,000,000."
2) Indemnity (narrow): "Vendor will indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging infringement of issued patents or copyrights arising solely from Vendor’s implementation of the Service. Customer will indemnify Vendor for claims arising from Customer-provided data or instructions."
3) Data training: "Vendor will not use Customer Data for model training or to improve any model without Customer’s prior written consent."
4) Subprocessors: "Vendor will provide notice of new subprocessors 30 days prior and will comply with the same data protection obligations as set forth in this Agreement. Customer may reasonably object to a new subprocessor on legitimate security or regulatory grounds."

Quick negotiation gameplan (15–30m sprint):
- 0–5m: scan contract for red flags (liability, indemnity, training, residency, termination). Mark each with A/B/C priority (A = must escalate).
- 5–15m: apply template snippets for A items and propose middle-ground for B items. Document concessions in legal ticket.
- 15–25m: draft micro scripts for AE/CS to explain changes and ask for commercial rationale behind aggressive asks.
- 25–30m: if unresolved A items remain, prepare escalation note (include revenue, customer tier, risk summary).

Random reminders (personal):
- Keep a separate folder of precedent language that got approved for high-risk customers.
- After final sign, update the clause-pattern library so peers can faster copy the right variant.

Endnotes: this doc is a personal sprint scratchpad not to be redistributed as final legal guidance. Replace placeholders (e.g., $1,000,000) with finance-approved numbers when escalating.

Unresolved / TODO:
- Confirm if we accept reciprocal indemnity for model hallucination damages (discuss with applied-ml).
- Standardize export templates with platform team.
- Get ops checklist for on-site limited evidence sharing (if needed).
